beats_top.query: cornell grad student stipend cost of living Ithaca enough
beats_top.why: Results are rate tables (Cornell Graduate School) and 2016 to 2023 Sun op-eds, none of which set the 2026-27 stipend against rent, the summer gap and what the health plan saves. Our opening paragraph answers the question with numbers and the rent table says what is left. It stops at rent: a grad deciding if the stipend is enough also wants food, transport, and a rough all-in monthly budget.
changes: Add a rough non-rent monthly cost line (groceries, phone, transport, other) with official or clearly sourced numbers, so 'left per month' becomes a real budget not just stipend minus rent.
Replace newspaper-only hard facts (union fee, TCAT subsidy, dental/vision) with official sources or drop them from the numbers.
Replace or support the Zumper market rent with a clearer local source, and state the real rent range for a shared two-bedroom.

fixes: Replace the op-ed link for the 30 percent rent-burden rule with an official source: cite HUD (https://www.hud.gov/ on housing cost burden, i.e. paying more than 30 percent of income on housing) and keep the op-ed only for what Nizalowska argued.

In the union fee bullet, replace the Cornell Sun as the source of the 1.44 percent fee with the official CGSU contract or a Cornell HR/Graduate School page, and recompute on the 2026-27 minimum ($48,912 x 1.44% = about $704 a year, about $59 a month), or if no official source can be found, remove the dollar figure and say only that a union fee exists, attributed to the Sun.

Source the 100 percent TCAT pass subsidy and the dental and vision coverage to the official CGSU contract or a Cornell/TCAT page with its conditions, or label both clearly as 'reported by the Sun, check the contract' and remove them from the 'If you are...' advice.
Source the charity-donation option for union fees to the official contract or drop it.

In the 'What students say' paragraph, remove 'during the pandemic' from the 12.3 percent sentence, since the column text gives no period; write 'cited a study showing Tompkins County rents rose 12.3 percent'.

Add a short section 'What is left after rent' with a rough monthly estimate for groceries, phone and transport, each linked to an official or clearly sourced number (for example the Tompkins County Workers' Center living wage study at https://www.tcworkerscenter.org/2026/04/tompkins-county-living-wage-updated-now-25-08-hour-detailed-study/ or Cornell's graduate cost-of-attendance page), labelled as an estimate.

Add a second market-rent source, for example a Cornell Graduate School or off-campus housing page or Apartments.com listings page, alongside the Zumper numbers, and state in the table row that Zumper's studio ($1,725) is above its one-bedroom ($1,695), which is a thin sample.
